new_entities.name: Phone ownership before age 10
new_entities.description: Owning or acquiring a smartphone or similar personal phone before 10 years of age.

new_entities.name: Adolescent mental health
new_entities.description: Mental health and psychological wellbeing outcomes in adolescents.

edges.effect_quant: Large early-adolescent cohort data show that younger age of smartphone acquisition is linked to worse health outcomes, and companion adolescent observational studies tie heavier smartphone exposure to more depressive symptoms, sleep problems, and psychological distress.
edges.population: children transitioning into adolescence, especially early adolescents with personal smartphone ownership
edges.mechanism: Earlier phone ownership can increase sustained exposure to social comparison, notifications, disrupted sleep, compulsive use loops, and displacement of offline recovery time during a sensitive developmental window.
edges.summary: The current evidence supports a cautious harmful classification for very early phone ownership, mainly because earlier acquisition is associated with worse mental-health-related outcomes in large adolescent cohorts. This is still an observational literature, so the right framing is risk signal rather than deterministic harm.
edges.caveats: Reverse causation, family context, baseline vulnerability, and broader digital environment all matter. The literature is stronger for associations with depressive symptoms, sleep disruption, and wellbeing than for proving that early phone ownership alone causes later psychiatric illness.

evidence.notes: Smartphone Ownership, Age of Smartphone Acquisition, and Health Outcomes in Early Adolescence.

evidence.citation: Kim Y and Oh H 2026 J Affect Disord
evidence.notes: Smartphone use, sleep, and mental health in Korean adolescents.
